(1) the mother-infant dyad is a dynamic, bidirectional system, (2) the mother's contingent coordination with the infant's behavior is greater than the infant's coordination with the mother's behavior, and (3) each partner's self-contingent organization of behavior is related to the partner's interactive coordination with the other.
(a) the infant and mother are each highly self-organized in their behavior and (b) the degree of self-organization is related to the degree to which each person coordinates with the other.

the dynamic, self- and interactive organization of communication in mother-infant face to face interaction.
the dynamic, bidirectional, self-organizing, and homoeostatic nature of mother-infant interaction.
how self- and interactive organization in face-to-face communication are interrelated in the context of a dynamic, bidirectional, dyadic process.

mother-infant communication is characterized by a dynamic, dyadically interrelated, self-organizing, homoeostatically balanced process of self-contingency and interactive contingency.
mother-infant communication is a complex, bidirectional, dynamic system in which self- and interactive contingencies are organized by a homoeostatic, bidirectional, and asymmetrical process.
the mother-infant dyad is a dynamic, dyadically interrelated, self-organizing system.

mother-infant face to-face communication is a self-organizing process that is simultaneously interactive.

we need to understand both the self-organizing and interactive processes of the infant and mother in order to better understand the dyadic process of mother-infant communication.
